title: Audit Handoff Orchestration: multipart uploads, provenance manifests, and customer-managed blobstores for VPC/On-Prem
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem statement:
Customers deploying Redwood Private in VPC or air-gapped on-prem environments require a reliable, resumable way to receive audit logs into their own blobstores (S3/GCS/Azure Blob/Ceph) while preserving cryptographic provenance (signed manifests) and respecting customer-managed retention policies and CMEK lifecycles. Current one-shot upload flows degrade for large daily archives and lack explicit artifact provenance for downstream compliance teams.

Goals:
- Implement an orchestrated handoff that supports multipart/resumable uploads to customer-managed object stores behind private networking (VPC endpoints or on-prem connectors).
- Produce a signed provenance manifest per batch (hashes, generation metadata, signer key id, timestamp) that customers can use to verify integrity on their side.
- Integrate with customer KMS/CMEK handshake for envelope encryption where applicable, without exposing keys to Redwood control plane.
- Provide operator controls to tune retention, rotate temporary credentials, and monitor partial upload states in Redwood Console/CLI.
- Ensure end-to-end auditability and observability (metrics and traces) while maintaining SLOs for audit delivery.

Non-goals:
- Replacing existing streaming syslog/forwarder integrations. This ticket focuses on batched archive handoff for Private/VPC and on-prem airgap export flows.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Orchestration service can initiate a batch export and coordinate multipart upload sessions with a customer-provided pre-signed URL or temporary credentials (STS) for S3-compatible stores and equivalent flows for GCS/Azure.
2) Each completed batch produces a signed provenance manifest (JSON) containing: batch_id, object list with SHA256, compression metadata, creator (redwood-agent id), upload completion timestamp, signer key fingerprint. Manifests are signed using a customer-accepted signing key (customer-supplied or Redwood ephemeral with customer-verified cert).
3) Uploads support resume/retry semantics and can gracefully handle network interruptions between Redwood export worker and the customer endpoint. Partial attempts are visible in Console and via export API.
4) Customers can optionally request CMEK-wrapped objects via an out-of-band KMS handshake flow; Redwood must not persist unwrapped keys.
5) End-to-end tests (unit + integration) and a runbook for operator recovery exist, with dashboards (upload success rate, latency P95, orphaned multipart parts) added to Console.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Two coordination models considered: (A) Redwood provides pre-signed multipart URLs and orchestrates part uploads from our workers; (B) Redwood uploads to an intermediate managed staging store and then triggers a customer-side pull. Model A reduces storage duplication and provides lower latency but requires robust temporary credential handling and more complex retry orchestration across private networks. We are implementing Model A as the default with an opt-in Model B for customers who cannot allow outbound connections from Redwood workers to their stores.
- Signing: Prefer customer-provided signing key (customer owns verification) to reduce trust surface. For customers unable to manage a key, Redwood can use ephemeral signing keys and provide a CA-signed verification certificate pinned by the customer for audits.
- CMEK: Supporting customer KMS introduces complexity across providers and on-prem HSMs. We'll define a minimal handshake (KMS key id + envelope-token exchange) that is pluggable per-provider and scope it to initial providers (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HashiCorp Vault).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Export-orchestrator service: new component in private-control-plane that coordinates lifecycle for batched exports, tracks part state, and emits events to Console.
2) Multipart upload adapter: provider-agnostic adapter that can create pre-signed URLs or STS creds for S3, GCS signed-posts, Azure Shared Access Signatures, and Ceph-compatible endpoints.
3) Provenance signer: signing interface that accepts either customer-supplied signer endpoint (HTTP webhook with mTLS) or Redwood ephemeral signer.
4) Resume/cleanup worker: cleans orphaned multipart uploads after a configurable TTL and surfaces operator actions.
5) Console/CLI: UI for export configuration (target URI, retention policy, CMEK handshake option), monitoring page for in-flight exports, and manual retry controls.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for adapter logic and manifest generation.
- Integration tests running in a staging VPC with a mock S3 endpoint (minio) and a simulated on-prem connector to validate resume behavior and TTL cleanup.
- Security review of signing key flows and CMEK handshake.

Rollout strategy:
- Phase 1 (internal beta): enable for Redwood-managed test tenants and the internal security team.
- Phase 2 (early customers): opt-in for 3 pilot customers across AWS/GCP/on-prem.
- Phase 3 (general availability): feature flag removed, documentation published, migration runbooks provided.

Metrics to monitor:
- batch_export_success_rate (per-customer)
- multipart_resume_rate and multipart_abort_count
- average_time_to_completion P50/P95
- orphaned_parts_count and storage_saved_by_direct_handoff

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Existing single-shot upload flows remain supported. New orchestration is opt-in with a per-customer config toggle. We will provide a migration tool to convert existing daily archives into the orchestrated multipart flow with provenance manifests.

Open questions / risks:
- Customers with strict egress policies may require model B (pull). Need operator docs for orchestrating customer-side pulls.
- Key rotation semantics for customer-supplied signing keys and how to surface revocation events.
- Latency impact on SLOs for audit delivery when orchestrating many simultaneous multipart sessions.

Next steps:
- Architect spike for multipart adapter and provenance schema (owner: Luis Martinez).
- Draft API surface for export orchestration and manifest format (owner: Priya Shah).
- Schedule security review with Platform Security (target: 2026-02-26).

2026-02-25 Security Review: Requested clearer spec for signing key ownership and KMS envelope flow. Security requested threat model and key rotation plan.
2026-03-03 QA: Integration tests showing resume success after worker restart (3/3 attempts). Noted flakiness when part upload latency > 30s — adding exponential backoff and jitter.
2026-03-07 Design feedback (Evan Cho): Add operator button to force-abort and trigger cleanup for orphaned parts. Also recommended adding a per-customer concurrency cap to protect downstream stores.
